Because the consequential output of such a system is an executed action rather than a paragraph, static text benchmarks such as HELM leave several failure modes unmeasured: demographic bias in discrete tool selection, unhandled runtime exceptions, corrupted transaction state, cascading multi-agent delusion, and a measurement artifact that inflates apparent bias whenever the fairness null is computed at the wrong group arity. This review synthesizes 59 sources into four governance pillars. Under action-space fairness auditing we set out the Bias Conduction Framework, Counterfactual Flip Rates, Mean Absolute Score Disparity, and the extreme-value expansion E[∆ K ] ≈ 2σ √ 2 ln K that AgentFairBench adopts as its null, and we show that this asymptotic form is loose at audit-scale group counts, deriving an exact arity mismatch factor of 2.25× for a six-group audit scored against a two-run baseline. Resource-efficient safety screening on commodity CPUs (TriEval) forms the second pillar. The third contrasts open-loop scaffolds such as ReAct and Toolformer against closed-loop architectures enforcing Abstract Syntax Tree schema validation, sandboxed execution, and transactional rollba…
